analysis:
Both units are base-side text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The head changes are documentation-only: a date bump at line 3, a new `addon` command row near line 156, and a new `darkbloom addon` section after the idle section (head lines 904-932). The section describes operator debugging of add-on holds (status/hold/release) through the provider's owner-only lifecycle mailbox, bound to the live process identity. It also says add-ons use a local socket documented in addon-hold-ipc.md.

The patch excerpt is truncated, so the full head section and the linked architecture/reference docs (addon-hold.md, addon-hold-ipc.md) were not supplied. The unit text also stops at base line 1725, so the head line 1758 change is unseen.

Security-relevant questions for later passes, which this docs-only change does not establish:
- Whether the add-on hold, mailbox and local socket are implemented in code. This PR touches only docs in the supplied evidence, so no code regression can be asserted.
- Whether hold semantics affect drain, stop, restart or serving authorization (TB-011, T-053, T-057). A hold could delay drain or keep the provider from serving, so the effect on availability and on A-016 authorization needs checking.
- Whether the local socket is authenticated and owner-only (TB-003). VMs and add-ons running beside the provider may affect memory and isolation (TB-007, T-014).

The base text itself has no changed-security content in the ranges supplied. The new feature may call for a threat-model update, such as a trust boundary for the add-on local socket, if the implementation exists. I cannot cite a concrete defect from this evidence, so there are no findings, but the truncated excerpt and unseen code justify a deeper-review flag.
